title: Chapter 57: She Has Arrived
html:
Their bodies swayed, filthy uniforms hanging from bloodless skin. Their mouths moved soundlessly, and their faces were frozen in terror. Each girl seemed to grow from the chair beneath her.

Chen Ge looked from the mirrors to the dressing-room entrance, cold spreading through his chest. Only minutes ago, he had tipped those chairs over and examined them.

Could that be considered my first intimate contact with a female?

A shudder passed through him, and he quickened his pace toward the door. The three chairs scraped forward in small increments while the lockers rattled behind him.

Everything in the studio had changed the moment he spoke Zhang Ya’s name. Here, that name was taboo.

The mirrors can only reflect what is in the dance studio. Perhaps there’s something even worse in the dressing room—I need to leave, pronto!

As if in answer, the steel locker doors creaked under pressure from within. Mallet in hand, Chen Ge charged the exit and kicked at the chairs blocking his path. As he tried to break through, something seized his shoulders.

In the mirror, two slender, pale arms hung over his shoulders. Chen Ge spun and attacked without hesitation.

Bang!

The mallet struck the chair’s back and split the wood. A woman’s scream pierced his ears. In the mirror, the student glared at him with naked hatred, her arms locked around his shoulders as she tried to force him into the seat.

Why is she doing this? Is this some kind of deadly game of musical chairs? If I sit down, will my soul be trapped inside forever?

More pale arms latched on to him. Their combined weight dragged him backward toward the dressing room. Then shuffling came from the outer corridor, and another wooden chair appeared in the studio entrance.

My luck is always used at the worst possible moment. It chooses a time like this to make me popular with the girls!

Driven to his limit, Chen Ge stopped trying to escape and went on the offensive. He gripped one chair by the back and swung the mallet with his other hand, laying waste to everything around him.

When the first crack appeared, the student’s pleading expression twisted into venomous hatred. That reaction gave Chen Ge his answer: the chairs were vessels, much like the rag dolls that housed Xiaoxiao’s family.

Destroying the objects they’re attached to won’t kill them, but it can at least hurt them.

The pressure intensified. Anyone less experienced might already have surrendered, but the girls had chosen the wrong victim. The Haunted House owner had survived a night in a cursed apartment with a serial killer. He still felt fear, but it no longer paralyzed him. Even in shock, he could think—and his grip on the mallet never wavered.

Bang!

He shattered the chair, seized one of its legs, and swung it at the next. The scene in the mirror defied description, and he had no time to contemplate it.

Within ten seconds, the first chair was destroyed. As he turned on the second, fingers closed around his throat. In the mirror, a pale hand tightened against his neck. The spirit had abandoned the attempt to seat him and decided to kill him instead.

The change only made Chen Ge more vicious. He seized the chairs and smashed them against the wall. With every crack, the pressure on his throat weakened. When all three lay in splinters, the hand finally vanished.

“Leaving these things here helps no one. Later, I’ll burn all of you so you can move on.” Chen Ge leaned against the mirror, struggling to catch his breath. Strangulation marks ringed his neck.

That fight made enough noise to attract whoever is following me. I need to leave now. The red dancing shoes clearly aren’t here anyway.

He had no desire to remain in the haunted studio. The lockers’ rattling grew violent—far beyond anything a draft could cause. The walls and floor seemed to darken, while a strange ping, ping from the corridor came faster and faster.

As he turned to leave, something caught his calf and nearly pulled him down.

The mirror showed all three students clinging to his leg, their nails digging into his skin.

Desperation took hold. He hammered the wooden fragments again and again, but the girls refused to release him.

The sound in the corridor drew closer. The girls’ hateful faces split into manic smiles. Darkness descended over the studio like a heavy cloth, warping his phone’s light, and the faint stench from earlier thickened until it filled the room.

Something even more terrifying is hiding in this school?

The thought terrified him. He had dared enter the school only because he believed Zhang Ya was its most dangerous presence. He was here to help her; she had no reason to hurt him.

This is bad.

Something reached the studio door. The stench became overwhelming.

The three girls glared up at him with savage expressions. Back pressed to the mirror, Chen Ge reached into his pocket. The instant his fingertip touched the doll, the sound at the door fled faster than it had approached. The stench receded with it.

What happened? It feels like the thing outside the door was scared.

Every unnatural sound ceased. Only his heartbeat remained. Yet his phone’s light twisted more violently than before, and the temperature plunged.

What is happening?

The hands released his calf. In the mirror, the three students had retreated as far as they could, staring in despair at the space behind him.

Behind me?

Slowly, stiffly, Chen Ge turned toward the full-length mirror. The reflection was not his own. A woman in a blood-red school uniform stood behind him, looking down.
